extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in civic improvement, practical invention promotion, and public-project organization (e.g., 18th-century citizens, inventors, civic leaders)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted evaluative principles and practical guidance embedded in Benjamin Franklin's autobiographical narrative about inventions, public-project promotion, municipal improvements, fundraising, and sectarian governance. These are informal norms and tactics for promoting inventions and public works rather than a formal modern patent rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of sharing inventions freely
rubrics_metrics.description: That, as we enjoy great advantages from the inventions of others, we should be glad of an opportunity to serve others by any invention of ours; and this we should do freely and generously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Franklin declines a patent for his stove from principle—valuing public benefit and reciprocity over personal exclusive profit. This is presented as an ethical stance toward invention dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk that publishing details allows others to patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An ironmonger in London, assuming a good deal of my pamphlet, and working it up into his own, and making some small changes in the machine... got a patent for it there, and made, as I was told, a little fortune by it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing full descriptions and drawings of an invention can enable others to appropriate, modify slightly, and obtain patents. Franklin notes this practical risk and that he generally did not contest such patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote inventions by writing clear explanatory pamphlets
rubrics_metrics.description: I wrote and published a pamphlet, entitled 'An Account of the new-invented Pennsylvania Fireplaces; wherein their Construction and Manner of Operation is particularly explained; their Advantages above every other Method of warming Rooms demonstrated; and all Objections that have been raised against the Use of them answered and obviated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A detailed pamphlet explaining construction, manner of operation, advantages, and answers to objections effectively promotes demand for an invention. Use clear demonstration and pre-emptive rebuttal of objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid self-promotion in public proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: In the introduction to these proposals, I stated their publication, not as an act of mine, but of some publick-spirited gentlemen, avoiding as much as I could, according to my usual rule, the presenting myself to the publick as the author of any scheme for their benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame proposals as coming from a public-spirited group rather than a single author to avoid alienating potential supporters and to encourage broader buy-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure subscriptions with yearly quotas to enlarge contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: it was to be paid in quotas yearly for five years; by so dividing it, I judg'd the subscription might be larger, and I believe it was so, amounting to no less... than five thousand pounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking required contributions into manageable recurring payments increases the willingness and ability of contributors to subscribe larger overall amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select trustees to prevent sectarian predominance
rubrics_metrics.description: It was therefore that one of each sect was appointed, viz., one Church-of-England man, one Presbyterian, one Baptist, one Moravian, etc., those, in case of vacancy by death, were to fill it by election from among the contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When fundraising and administering resources contributed by diverse groups, appoint trustees representing each group to avoid giving long-term control to any single sect or faction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use conditional legislative clauses to secure public funding and stimulate private giving
rubrics_metrics.description: I drew it so as to make the important clause a conditional one, viz., '...that when the said contributors shall have met and chosen their managers and treasurer, and shall have raised by their contributions a capital stock of ------ value... that then it shall and may be lawful for the said speaker... to sign an order... for the payment of two thousand pounds...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft public-funding legislation with clear conditional requirements (e.g., demonstrate matched private capital) so the legislature can support without sole fiscal burden and private donors are motivated by matching public funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish sample demonstrations to persuade public and official adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: The honour of this public benefit has also been ascrib'd to me, but it belongs truly to that gentleman. I did but follow his example, and have only some merit to claim respecting the form of our lamps, as differing from the globe lamps we were at first supply'd with from London. Those we found inconvenient...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tangible demonstrations or local examples (e.g., a working street lamp) to convince the public and authorities of the utility of a proposed improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use lists of subscribers and solicit broadly to increase donations
rubrics_metrics.description: I advise you to apply to all those whom you know will give something; next, to those whom you are uncertain whether they will give any thing or not, and show them the list of those who have given; and, lastly, do not neglect those who you are sure will give nothing, for in some of them you may be mistaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish and show lists of prior donors to create social proof; solicit everyone including uncertain and unlikely donors since some will contribute unexpectedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal street-cleaning tactic: sweep early and coordinate via watchmen
rubrics_metrics.description: "For the more effectual cleaning and keeping clean the streets... it is proposed that the several watchmen be contracted with to have the dust swept up in dry seasons, and the mud rak'd up at other times... That in the dry summer months the dust be all swept up into heaps at proper distances, before the shops and windows of houses are usually opened..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule sweeping before shops open, contract local patrol/watchmen to organize sweeping, provide tools at stands, and collect swept dust in covered carts for removal to reduce dust and mud nuisance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Street drainage design: single central gutter
rubrics_metrics.description: Here let me remark the convenience of having but one gutter in such a narrow street, running down its middle, instead of two, one on each side... it forms there a current strong enough to wash away all the mud it meets with; but when divided into two channels, it is often too weak to cleanse either.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design narrow streets with a single central gutter to create a stronger self-cleansing current rather than divided side channels that are less effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Street-lamp design improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: I therefore suggested the composing them of four flat panes, with a long funnel above to draw up the smoke, and crevices admitting air below, to facilitate the ascent of the smoke; by this means they were kept clean, and did not grow dark in a few hours...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple flat panes rather than globe lamps, add a funnel to draw smoke upward, and provide lower air inlets to maintain bright illumination and ease of repair (replace single pane rather than entire globe).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mud-collection cart design (low draining sleds)
rubrics_metrics.description: that the scavengers be provided with bodies of carts, not plac'd high upon wheels, but low upon sliders, with lattice bottoms, which, being cover'd with straw, will retain the mud thrown into them, and permit the water to drain from it, whereby it will become much lighter... these bodies of carts to be plac'd at convenient distances...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect wet mud in low, draining sled-like receptacles with lattice bottoms to allow water to drain before transport, reducing transport weight. Franklin notes practical doubts about narrow streets but presents the design concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate feasibility by local small-scale execution
rubrics_metrics.description: I bid her sweep the whole street clean, and I would give her a shilling; this was at nine o'clock; at 12 she came for the shilling... the whole street was swept perfectly clean... I then judg'd that, if that feeble woman could sweep such a street in three hours, a strong, active man might have done it in half the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove a concept's practicality by commissioning or demonstrating it on a small scale and using the result to persuade others of its feasibility and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid formalizing doctrines if future improvement is expected
rubrics_metrics.description: When we were first drawn together as a society... From time to time He has been pleased to afford us farther light, and our principles have been improving... Now we are not sure that we are arrived at the end of this progression... we fear that, if we should once print our confession of faith, we should feel ourselves as if bound and confin'd by it...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For organizations or movements that anticipate doctrinal or procedural evolution, avoid rigid printed confessions/rules that may hinder future improvement or lock successors into past positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting procedural tactic: delay vote to allow potential opposition/support to appear
rubrics_metrics.description: By our rules, no money could be dispos'd of till the next meeting after the proposal. ... When the hour for business arriv'd it was mov'd to put the vote; he allow'd we might then do it by the rules, but, as he could assure us that a number of members intended to be present for the purpose of opposing it, it would be but candid to allow a little time for their appearing... I went up, and after a little seeming hesitation, agreed to a delay of another hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use procedural delays strategically to allow absent members to arrive (or to reveal their absence), and to manage perceptions of fairness; absence can be used as indicative of tacit support or non-opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use moral/political phrasing to circumvent principled objections
rubrics_metrics.description: They were unwilling to offend government... and their friends... by a compliance contrary to their principles; hence a variety of evasions to avoid complying... The common mode at last was, to grant money under the phrase of its being 'for the king's use,' and never to inquire how it was applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When stakeholders have principled objections to explicit actions (e.g., Quakers and war), use neutral or generalized phrasing for appropriations (e.g., 'for the king's use') to obtain necessary resources while avoiding direct violation of professed principles.
